title: Rotting Oranges
keyIdea: Multi-source BFS: queue every rotten orange at time 0. Popping one at time t rots its fresh neighbours at t + 1. BFS order = time order, so each orange rots at the earliest minute. Any fresh orange left → −1; else the largest time.

approaches.name: DFS with time relaxation
approaches.idea: DFS from each rotten orange carrying the time; revisit a cell only if this path reaches it sooner.
approaches.why: A cell can be re-explored many times as faster paths arrive; correct but wasteful.

approaches.name: Multi-source BFS
approaches.idea: Queue all rotten oranges with time 0; pop, rot fresh neighbours at time + 1, push them; track the max time; check for leftover fresh ones.
approaches.why: Every cell enters the queue at most once.

quiz.q: Why put ALL rotten oranges in the queue at the start?
options: Rot spreads from all of them at once; starting together makes BFS layers equal to minutes

quiz.q: Why does BFS give the minimum time?
options: It processes cells in order of time, so the first time a cell is reached is the earliest
When a fresh orange is never reached by any rotten one
When there are no rotten oranges and no fresh ones

quiz.q: Can plain DFS (mark once, never revisit) give the right time?
options: No: it may reach a cell first by a long path and never fix it
